extracted.intended_audience: authors and journal editors of patient safety and quality improvement (QI) studies; healthcare researchers reporting QI work
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for how to write and report patient safety and quality improvement (QI) studies so that they are clear, comparable, and useful to clinicians, researchers, and journal editors. Focused on the SQUIRE 2.0 standards for publication reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different standard of evaluation for QI studies
rubrics_metrics.description: QI studies demand a different standard of evaluation than traditional biomedical research, given their complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and account for the complexity of QI work when choosing study design and reporting approaches rather than applying evaluation standards designed for conventional biomedical research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous evaluation to avoid harm and waste
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to rigorously evaluate QI research could result in wasted resources and unanticipated consequences if poorly evaluated interventions are widely implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure rigorous evaluation methods are used and clearly reported so that interventions are not adopted prematurely or without evidence of benefit and safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a blueprint for reporting QI results
rubrics_metrics.description: These guidelines provide a blueprint for reporting the results of QI studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SQUIRE as a standardized framework to structure reports of QI and patient safety studies so that methods, context, interventions, and outcomes are clearly and consistently described for readers and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usability and avoidance of confusing sub-items
rubrics_metrics.description: SQUIRE 2.0 improves the usability of the guidelines and omits the multiple sub-items that were felt to be too confusing for authors in the initial document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer clearer, more usable checklist items over many detailed sub-items; emphasis on practical usability for authors preparing manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consensus-based, transparent guideline development
rubrics_metrics.description: SQUIRE 2.0 was revised through a process that included semistructured interviews, focus groups, consensus meetings, pilot testing with authors, and a public comment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality reporting guidelines should be developed using inclusive, transparent, and iterative methods (e.g., stakeholder interviews, focus groups, pilot testing, and public comment) to enhance legitimacy and applicability.
